headline: CISA warns a critical Cisco Expressway RCE flaw is being actively exploited
summary: CISA has warned federal agencies that attackers are exploiting a recently patched critical remote code execution flaw in Cisco Expressway. The source does not give the CVE identifier or details about the attacks.

headline: Critical Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 exploited after PoC release, internal network reached
summary: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) in Cisco Expressway shortly after a public proof-of-concept appeared. They breached four devices at a Russian organization and reached its internal network. The flaw is reported to let an unauthenticated remote attacker with network access compromise the device.

headline: FBI investigates possible cyberattack on National Crime Information Center
summary: The FBI is investigating a possible cyberattack on the NCIC, a key US national police database. Reports say the FBI appears to have been targeted again, but the extent of any compromise has not been confirmed.

headline: N-able discloses critical SSRF in Mail Assure found during breach investigation
summary: N-able disclosed CVE-2026-134624, an SSRF flaw found while it was investigating a breach of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud email filtering service for MSPs. The flaw let users with high-level API access open connections to internal systems they chose.

headline: Norway says Microsoft cloud flaw was exploited against energy firms Equinor and Skagerak Energi
summary: Norway's cybersecurity authorities say attackers exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft's cloud to go after sensitive credentials. Energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi were affected.

summary: Researchers describe a PHP vulnerability called phpAfterShell that reopens the attack path used by PHP2Shell. If a session overwrite is interrupted, an attacker who controls the new data may be able to trigger deserialization and run code remotely. The source does not mention any exploitation in the wild or a CVE.

summary: Microsoft has confirmed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft Entra Connect Health, and the incident is described as a data leak. The source does not give a CVE, the scope of the exposed data or the affected tenants.

summary: Flaws in SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway are reported as exploited in attacks. Attackers can use them to leak or modify server information and to execute commands as root. The source excerpt names no CVEs or actors.

headline: N-able patches critical flaw disclosed after Mail Assure cyberattack
summary: N-able has patched a critical flaw that was disclosed after a cyberattack on its Mail Assure email security service. The company says access to the affected services has been restored and it is still monitoring the environments. The source does not give a CVE or technical details.

headline: Critical code injection flaw in the binary-parser JavaScript library (CVE-2026-134814)
summary: Versions of the binary-parser library before 2.3.1 allow code injection when an attacker controls the parser definitions. The flaw is rated CVSS 9.2/8.1, and no exploitation has been reported.

headline: GreyNoise reports intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers
summary: GreyNoise reports an intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers. It confirmed attack activity between 17 October and 2 November 2026 affecting at least 22 organisations worldwide. The source gives no vulnerability or attacker details.

headline: Critical flaw in legacy ASP.NET Idunno.AntiCsrf library exploited for unauthenticated RCE
summary: CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS 9.3) affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta of the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library for ASP.NET. Researchers report it has been exploited in the wild and can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. They recommend stopping use of the library altogether.

headline: Cleverbridge e-commerce platform breach exposes payment card numbers and CVVs
summary: Cleverbridge, a payments and subscription platform used by software vendors, has confirmed that attackers stole card data, including CVV codes, after it detected unauthorised activity on 4 November 2026. It has not said which merchant clients' customers were affected.

headline: German payment platform Cleverbridge reports theft of card data and security codes
summary: Dutch-language coverage reports that the German payment platform Cleverbridge suffered a cyberattack in which sensitive card data, including security codes, was stolen. The source gives limited detail.

headline: Attackers exploited GL.iNet GoodCloud flaw to plant malware on routers and KVM devices
summary: GL.iNet says attackers exploited a vulnerability in its GoodCloud remote management service to install malware on some customer routers and KVM devices. The company says it fixed the flaw and blocked the attacker's access, so devices can no longer be infected this way. It has not said how many devices were affected.

headline: GL.iNet routers and KVMs compromised through a flaw in the GoodCloud remote management service
summary: Attackers abused a flaw in GL.iNet's GoodCloud cloud management service to push malware to routers and KVM devices. Cleaning affected devices requires new firmware.

headline: Cleverbridge confirms breach of customer payment card data, including security codes
summary: E-commerce payment provider Cleverbridge has confirmed a breach of customer payment card data. Stolen data reportedly includes card numbers and security codes it had stored, which puts affected individuals at immediate risk of fraud. The source does not give the number of people affected.

headline: GL.iNet confirms cloud management flaw exploited to backdoor routers and KVM devices
summary: GL.iNet has confirmed that attackers exploited a flaw in its cloud remote management service to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices. Some affected users report backdoors and reverse shells that give attackers remote access. The source names no CVE.

headline: GL.iNet GoodCloud management service compromised to push malware to routers and KVM devices
summary: Attackers compromised GoodCloud, GL.iNet's cloud remote-management service. They used it to install malware on routers and KVM devices that were connected to it. The number of affected devices is still unknown while the vendor investigates, and separate research by a partner and by users reportedly found older backdoors.

headline: BadBox 3.0 ad fraud and residential proxy operation on backdoored consumer devices disrupted
summary: The BadBox 3.0 operation used backdoors on low-cost consumer devices to deliver modules for ad fraud and to turn the devices into residential proxies. At its peak it generated about 40 billion bid requests a day before being disrupted. The source excerpt does not say who carried out the disruption.

headline: US lawmakers propose cyber incident review board within CISA
summary: Two members of the US Congress have put forward a bill that would set up a board inside CISA to review major cyber incidents. The proposal is not yet law, and the source does not give details on the board's scope or timing.

headline: CERT-In warns of AI-assisted attacks causing unauthorized transactions at Indian financial firms
summary: India's CERT-In has warned that threat actors are using AI-assisted techniques to attack ICT assets in the country. According to the advisory, the activity has led to unauthorized financial transactions at banks, financial services firms and technology service providers. The source does not give technical details or name any victims.

headline: Dragos reports undetected intrusions and prompt theft at three AI inference providers
summary: Dragos says it found intrusions at three AI inference providers that the providers themselves had not detected, with nearly two million prompts sent to AI services involved. The excerpt suggests customer prompts could have been exposed. The providers are not named.

headline: Signal moves to stop built-in iOS and Android AI agents from reading chats
summary: Signal has added protections to keep AI agents built into iOS and Android from reading its chats. It is also asking platform makers to provide an opt-out. This is a product change with no reported incident behind it.

headline: Signal restricts operating-system AI assistants from capturing message content
summary: Signal is blocking AI assistants built into mobile operating systems, including Siri AI on iOS 27 and Gemini on Android, from capturing what is on screen in conversations. Signal says these assistants could store message text in local databases or send it to remote servers.

headline: Bots impersonate AI agent identities to probe for exposed secrets, Cequence reports
summary: Cequence reports that automated bots are using AI agent names, such as user-agent identifiers, to hide while they probe for secrets. The finding comes as AI agents move from reading data to taking actions. The source summary does not name victims, specific targets or regions.

headline: Chinese hackers reportedly used Cairn AI tool to find zero-days in attacks on Asian universities
summary: A Security.NL report says Chinese hackers used an AI tool called Cairn to find zero-day vulnerabilities while attacking several universities in Asia. The source excerpt does not name affected products, CVEs or detection guidance.

headline: Amazon: China-nexus actor used Cairn AI agents to exploit a zero-day in a medical imaging AI app
summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence says a China-nexus actor ran autonomous agents on the open-source Cairn AI pentesting framework against university servers. The agents had little human direction. After nearly a day of failed attempts, they found and exploited a zero-day in an open-source medical imaging AI application and gained a foothold.

headline: WPIDE WordPress plugin up to 3.6.4: CSRF nonce bypass enables unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-124251)
summary: WPIDE versions up to 3.6.4 check the nonce only when the page parameter is exactly "wpide". This undoes the earlier fix for CVE-2026-57766 and can lead to remote code execution through CSRF. No exploitation in the wild is reported.

headline: Badbox 3.0 botnet returns with ad fraud and proxyjacking payloads
summary: HUMAN Satori researchers report that a new Badbox 3.0 variant spreads ad fraud and proxyjacking payloads. The researchers say it generates about 40 billion bid requests a day.

headline: HUMAN disrupts BADBOX 3.0 ad fraud botnet of infected TV boxes that also act as proxies
summary: HUMAN's Satori team disrupted BADBOX 3.0, an operation that ran mainly on infected low-cost TV boxes. At its peak it generated about 40 billion ad bid requests a day. The infected devices also rent out their owners' home internet connections as proxies.

headline: Vendor commentary: AI agents create a shared-responsibility gap for identity and permissions
summary: Token Security argues that AI agents working across several platforms leave gaps that no single vendor can see or control. The piece recommends tighter management of agent identities, permissions and accountability. It is vendor-sponsored commentary.

headline: Trump expected to nominate Kirsten Davies as US national cyber director
summary: Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer and acting national cyber director, is reported to be the president's likely pick for the full nomination. The report says she has strong support.

headline: CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Zscaler in all-stock deal valued near $43.9 billion
summary: SecurityWeek, Help Net Security, Infosecurity Magazine: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion. Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share. The deal would combine endpoint and network security platforms. CyberScoop: The deal would combine endpoint protection and network access controls, and CrowdStrike is presenting it as part of a push to secure AI agents. The report does not describe any immediate security risk.

headline: Schneier essay argues AI chatbot output should not receive human speech rights
summary: In an essay, Bruce Schneier discusses a Florida court's decision in a wrongful-death lawsuit against Character.AI. The court rejected the company's arguments that chatbot output is protected speech and that its service falls outside product-liability law. Schneier argues that machines should not hold the rights that humans do.

headline: CrowdStrike announces acquisition of Zscaler for about $43.9 billion
summary: CrowdStrike says it will buy Zscaler for roughly $43.9 billion as part of building an integrated security platform. This is M&A news and does not create any immediate operational risk.

headline: Microsoft confirms Windows 11 hotpatch KB5132043 breaks printing on Forcepoint DLP systems
summary: Microsoft has confirmed that printing fails on some Windows 11 systems running Forcepoint DLP software after the November 2026 hotpatch KB5132043 is installed. This is a compatibility problem in an update, not a security vulnerability.

headline: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
summary: CrowdStrike plans to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion, bringing together two long-time partners. The deal is aimed at buyers who want to consolidate security vendors.

headline: SANS notes Debian/Ubuntu rsyslog config change affecting syslog timestamp formats
summary: A SANS ISC diary entry traces how syslog timestamp formats have changed over time. It notes that in early 2023 Debian and Ubuntu removed a configuration directive from their rsyslogd package, which can change the timestamp format that log pipelines receive.

headline: Journalist with no hunting experience uses free AI models to find WordPress plugin flaw
summary: A reporter with no prior bug-hunting experience used two free AI models to find and report a flaw in a WordPress plugin installed on more than 40,000 sites. It took about six hours. The piece shows how AI lowers the skill needed to discover vulnerabilities.

headline: Open-source AI pentest tool Xalgorix uses a second agent to verify findings
summary: Xalgorix is an open-source AI penetration testing tool. A second agent tries to exploit each bug the main agent finds again, to cut false positives. Findings that cannot be confirmed or ruled out are flagged for a person to review.

headline: Survey: Dutch people rate their digital skills highly, but knowledge and online behaviour lag
summary: A Dutch report finds that most people in the Netherlands see themselves as digitally skilled. However, their digital knowledge and online behaviour fall short in important areas. This points to ongoing awareness gaps.

headline: Peruvian call center operator sentenced to eight years for government-impersonation scam on 30,000 Americans
summary: A Peruvian call center operator received an eight-year prison sentence for his part in a years-long government-impersonation fraud. The scheme took millions of dollars from more than 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents.

headline: Weekly recap: VMware zero-day and several shell-access flaws in Java, NGINX and Ruby
summary: A weekly roundup from The Hacker News mentions a VMware zero-day and remote shell problems labelled Java4Shell, NGINX2Root and Ruby2Shell. The excerpt doesn't give CVEs, affected versions or confirmed details for any of them.

headline: Bits of Freedom calls Dutch DPA warning on camera glasses insufficient
summary: Dutch civil-rights group Bits of Freedom says the Dutch Data Protection Authority's (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) warning about camera glasses does not go far enough. The dispute is about privacy risks from wearable recording devices.

headline: Sponsored piece urges leaders to assess where AI changes intrusion cost, speed and scale
summary: This sponsored opinion piece says security leaders should stop asking whether AI can run a whole attack. It argues they should look at where AI makes intrusions cheaper, faster or larger. It reports no specific incident or vulnerability.

headline: Dutch police launch fake webshop awareness campaign against online shopping fraud
summary: Dutch police launched a public awareness campaign using Deckdeals.nl, a decoy website offering cheap Pokémon cards. The campaign aims to show consumers how easily they can fall for webshop fraud.

headline: CVE-2026-129975: double free in status line read code listed by Amazon Linux
summary: Amazon Linux Security Center lists CVE-2026-129975, a double-free bug in status line read code. The record doesn't name the affected component and doesn't confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch exists.

headline: Italian cancer institute's digital chief on hospital resilience and shadow IT in research
summary: The digital transformation director of Italy's Istituto Nazionale Tumori talks about keeping clinical operations running and protected from cyberattacks. He covers working with partner hospitals, why banning shadow IT in research rarely helps, and the burden of EU regulation.

headline: Sponsored piece argues AI security and post-quantum cryptography belong on one roadmap
summary: This sponsored article argues that AI security and post-quantum cryptography should be planned together, not treated as competing budget priorities. It reports no incident or new vulnerability.

headline: Sponsored piece outlines enterprise security shifts driven by AI and quantum computing
summary: This sponsored article describes five shifts it says should push organisations toward AI accountability and post-quantum readiness. It contains no new incident or regulatory development.

headline: Mozilla criticizes Apple's requirements for third-party browser engines on iOS
summary: Mozilla has publicly criticized the conditions Apple sets for browsers that want to use their own engine on iOS. In practice, iPhone browsers still run on Apple's engine. This is a platform-policy dispute, not a security incident.

headline: SANS ISC Stormcast daily podcast for 23 November 2026
summary: SANS ISC has published its daily Stormcast podcast episode. The source gives no details about which topics it covers.

headline: Microsoft testing a fix for Bluetooth audio quality drops in Windows 11
summary: Microsoft is testing a fix for a long-standing Windows 11 issue that degrades audio quality on Bluetooth headphones. This is a functional bug, not a security issue.

headline: Developer blog shares AI-built page comparing HTML select box styling
summary: A developer blog post presents a tool page, built with an AI assistant, that shows different ways to style HTML select boxes across browsers. It has no security content.
